title: Abdominal ultrasound for children
what: The doctor uses ultrasound to look at your child's belly organs: liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, and kidneys. It is safe and painless.
why: If your child has belly pain, poor weight gain, vomiting, or abnormal test results; or at a checkup.
duration: usually 10 to 20 minutes; the report is ready right away
tell_doctor: What bothers your child and for how long
What medicines your child takes now
If your child had belly surgery

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually fasting. Babies: before their next feed. Older children: 4 to 6 hours without food. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Drinks
prepare.text: Plain water is usually fine. No soda or juice.

prepare.title: Mindset
prepare.text: Tell your child it will feel cool and a little ticklish, but it will not hurt.

bring: A toy or a cartoon on your phone, to distract your child
steps: Your child lies on their back, and you stay close
Gel is put on the belly
The doctor moves the probe over the belly
Sometimes your child is asked to turn on their side or take a deep breath
The gel is wiped off with a tissue
feel: Young children may cry. That is normal, and the doctor will wait
after: You can feed your child right after the scan
The report is usually ready right away
Go over the results with your pediatrician

faq.q: Can I feed my child before the ultrasound?
faq.a: Usually not. The organs are easier to see on an empty stomach. Babies: before their next feed.
No. Ultrasound uses no radiation. It is done even on newborns.

reminders.text: Your child's abdominal ultrasound is tomorrow. It is usually done fasting. Check the time with the clinic. Bring a sheet.
